doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

chapter: Career, recognition and jazz in America
title: Entertaining the audience versus playing with the head
summary: Asked if critics dislike his showmanship, he says he wants people to have a good time and criticizes overly complicated jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You said something just in passing there, that you have, part of what you do involves respect for the audience. And I wonder if the reason that you don’t show up, especially in the critics’ poll, is partly because of that. In other words there’s an entertainment part of your performances which is inviting to people, and sometimes critics feel like oh that’s not really artistic. That’s a little too much show business.

Okay. If they believe so that’s their problem. My intention is to make the people have a good time. And you know a famous pianist, I’m not going to name his name, it’s not necessary, but he posted something a couple of days [inaudible] in that what he said: people nowadays in the jazz music — exactly, I’m quoting — he’s a famous jazz pianist. He said people nowadays play with their head but not with the soul. And I said you know I was tempted to reply to that. I said you shouldn’t generalize you know. You shouldn’t put everything on everybody in the same sack because that’s not fair. But sometimes in a certain way he’s right because a lot of jazz musicians make it so complicated nowadays and so technical and so intricate that avoids to gain a lot more people who appreciate, understand and follow jazz music. And that’s one of the things I’m not looking for. I don’t want to impress the people. I want the people to have a good time. And leave the place with the desire to come back when I get back in town. That’s the way to make our business survive.
